description:
## Why (placeholder)

OS-native trust stores are the most common non-file trust source in deployment. macOS, Windows, iOS, and Android all expose trust roots through platform APIs whose on-disk representation is platform-private. This is the `rustls-native-certs` analog for the `pkix-truststore` ecosystem.

## Scope

Adapter crate that calls platform-native APIs and returns `Vec<TrustAnchor>` via `pkix_truststore::from_der_iter(...)`. Per-platform feature flags; one crate, multiple targets.

Platforms in scope:
- macOS — `security-framework` crate (Security.framework / Keychain)
- Windows — `windows-sys` (CryptoAPI: `CertOpenSystemStore`, `CertEnumCertificatesInStore`)
- iOS — Security framework (mirror of macOS)
- Android — `KeyStore` API via JNI (open question: which JNI binding crate)
- Linux/BSD — file-path discovery (`/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` and distro variants); pure file reading, no FFI

## API shape (canonical adapter pattern)

```rust
// Returns the system trust store as a Vec<TrustAnchor>.
// Each platform feature compiles to a different implementation.
pub fn load() -> Result<Vec<TrustAnchor>, Error>;

// Re-export for ergonomics.
pub use pkix_truststore::TrustAnchor;

// Adapter-specific error wrapping platform errors.
pub enum Error {
    Platform(/* platform-specific */),
    Truststore(pkix_truststore::Error),
    Unsupported,  // target platform has no implementation
}
```

Implementation per platform:
1. Call platform API to enumerate trust certs.
2. Extract DER for each.
3. Pass `Vec<DER>` through `pkix_truststore::from_der_iter(...)`.
4. Return result.

## Dependencies (per platform feature)

- `pkix-truststore` (workspace) — for `from_der_iter` and `TrustAnchor` re-export
- `security-framework` — macOS/iOS feature
- `windows-sys` — Windows feature
- (Android JNI binding — TBD)

## Out of scope

- Trust policy / per-anchor flags (NSS-style "trusted for serverAuth only" — Apple does have this in Security framework but matching it requires extending `pkix-path::TrustAnchor`).
- Real-time trust store change watching.
- macOS `SecTrustSettings*` per-domain trust overrides (system-wide store only for the initial implementation of this adapter).

## Status

PLACEHOLDER. No implementation work scheduled. File concrete sub-beads when a consumer requests this adapter or when the architectural pattern needs validation against a real platform integration.

## Relates to

- PKIX-lhm4 (`pkix-truststore` Tier 1 core).
notes:
Placeholder bead per architectural conversation 2026-05-08. Records the canonical adapter pattern (API call → DER bytes → from_der_iter → Vec<TrustAnchor>) and pins the per-platform feature-flag layout. No work scheduled.
Marked blocked 2026-05-10: bead is explicitly labelled '(placeholder)' in its title and starts with '## Why (placeholder)'. This is a scope-capture stub, not a unit of immediate work. Unblock when there is a concrete consumer requiring OS-native trust store integration.
Stub crate created 2026-05-11: pkix-truststore-system/ exists with empty skeleton at 0.1.0, ready for namespace publication. Substantive content per this bead's description (per-platform trust store readers for macOS / Windows / iOS / Android) remains the open work.

When the platform readers are implemented, the anticipatory pkix-truststore dep and platform-specific deps (security-framework, wincert-store, JNI) get added to the stub crate's Cargo.toml at that time.
Escalating to human (do-beads loop, 2026-05-11): bead description explicitly says 'Status: PLACEHOLDER. No implementation work scheduled. File concrete sub-beads when a consumer requests this adapter or when the architectural pattern needs validation against a real platform integration.' Autonomously expanding into concrete per-platform adapter work would violate that explicit gating. Decision needed:

  (a) Keep as tracking-only placeholder and re-label / defer so it stops surfacing as ready every session.
  (b) Expand into concrete sub-beads now for a specific platform — Linux/BSD file-path discovery is the lowest-risk Tier-1 target (pure file reading, no FFI, no per-platform feature flags needed), and would actually be the consumer pattern PKIX-zydl's fixture-refresh procedure documented.
  (c) Close as documented-API-skeleton and reopen if / when a consumer asks.

Recommendation: (b) for Linux/BSD only, as a concrete first beachhead. The fixture work from PKIX-zydl (2026-05-10) already documented the per-distro file paths and verification approach. macOS / Windows / iOS / Android remain placeholders until a consumer surfaces or until Mark has a workstation to test against. The Linux/BSD slice is ~1 day of work: walk a list of candidate paths, parse via pkix_truststore::from_pem, return the first non-empty result, with feature flags for distro-specific path lists.
Relabeled 2026-05-11 (Mark): human → placeholder. Bead text already explicitly states "Status: PLACEHOLDER. No implementation work scheduled. File concrete sub-beads when a consumer requests this adapter or when the architectural pattern needs validation against a real platform integration." The human label was causing the bead to surface in the autonomous ready queue every session; the placeholder label expresses the same gating intent without the false signal that a maintainer decision is pending. Unblock by either:
  (a) a consumer asking for OS-native trust integration, or
  (b) a maintainer choosing to expand the Linux/BSD slice (pure file reading, ~1 day) as a concrete first beachhead.
Deferred to 2027-05-11 (Mark): the placeholder label correctly captures the bead nature but does NOT hide it from bd ready (only the human label does, and re-adding human is misleading because there is no pending maintainer decision — the gating condition is "wait for consumer"). Using bd defer hides it from the autonomous ready queue without faking a decision-pending state. Clear the defer manually if a consumer surfaces or if a maintainer chooses to expand the Linux/BSD slice as a beachhead.
